scope: research-only typed threshold relation integrity and opportunity coverage on live V6
material_findings: The current V6 threshold family key discards day-of-month while structural_intents assumes a one-dollar terminal payoff floor for paired threshold relations. Different expiries inside the same month/year can therefore be grouped even though the implication is not valid across dates.
The incumbent unsuffixed numeric ranking can choose the calendar year instead of an integer/count threshold.
The incumbent direction vocabulary does not recognize or-more/or-fewer constructions.
The incumbent optional b suffix can consume the first letter of the following word by, turning $100,000 by ... into a 1e14 threshold.
The live V6 intent guard currently rejects STRUCTURAL intents, so this is fail-closed for live paper but blocks safe structural opportunity coverage.

deterministic_counterexample.conclusion: Cross-expiry YES(low)+NO(high) has no guaranteed $1 payoff floor.

required_next_evidence: Run incumbent and typed relation parsers on the same chronological 300/700-market V6 public universe.
Report recovered valid same-expiry families, rejected cross-expiry families and candidate turnover.
Verify the logical payoff floor for every structural bundle before using structural edge.
Require positive executable economics after 1x, 1.5x and 2x cost/legging stress.
